body:
## Problem

Replay can wait for parent-context jobs queued behind ordinary pipeline jobs in other memory contexts. The watchdog previously observed only completions in the awaited context, so productive FIFO work could trigger a false timeout and crash recovery.

## What changes

Observe completed jobs across all memory contexts when resetting the existing monotonic no-progress deadline. Synchronization still waits for the requested context to drain. Add deterministic GPU-independent FIFO, true-stall, normal-completion and cancellation regressions, and document the corrected timeout semantics.

## Why this matters

Useful replay work no longer triggers recovery merely because its completions belong to a different memory context. A worker that stops completing work still reaches its configured deadline.

## Why this approach

Read the existing counters under the existing queue mutex and widen their sum to `uint64_t`. This keeps the correction within progress accounting while preserving queue ordering, heartbeat, cancellation, recovery, CLI options, public interfaces, formats and cache-marker policy.

## Verification and limits

- Linux Debug/Release × exceptions OFF/ON: all 222 registered CPU tests passed in each configuration; all 38 timeout tests passed three consecutive runs per configuration.
- Candidate-derived original-rule Debug/Release controls compile and reproduce the intended false timeout with one and two compilation threads; normal completion and genuine-stall controls pass.
- The independent work-unit checker reran the full four-configuration matrix and original-rule controls; a separate fresh final checker passed 47 decisive tests three times each in Debug and Release (282 executions), with no findings.
- [Independent work-unit report](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/harness-artifacts/runs/issue-70/issue70-20261103/reports/check-unit-1.json) and [separate final report](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/harness-artifacts/runs/issue-70/issue70-20261103/reports/check-final-1.json).
- Native Windows execution was explicitly waived as unavailable on this machine and remains unverified. These CPU fixtures establish no GPU, driver, Steam timing or output-durability result.

## Task references

Closes https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/70
